current_activity: organising defensive positions across the Cotentin
notes: VIII Corps (Middleton) operational 15 June west of Carentan to organise defensive positions across the Cotentin.

composing_units: 82nd Airborne Division; 90th Infantry Division; 101st Airborne Division
current_activity: taking control of 90th Division and 82nd Airborne
notes: Control of 90th Division and 82nd Airborne passed to VIII Corps 19 June to secure VII Corps south flank.

composing_units: 79th Infantry Division; 82nd Airborne Division; 90th Infantry Division; 101st Airborne Division
notes: 79th Division moved south 28 June to reorganise under VIII Corps for the drive south out of the Cotentin.

current_activity: exploiting the Cobra breakthrough toward Coutances
notes: Wikipedia: VIII Corps joined the Cobra breakout on 26 July, took Coutances on 28 July and Avranches two days later.

current_activity: taking Avranches and opening the Pontaubault gap
notes: Breakout-16: early on the evening of 30 July troops of the 4th Armored Division CCB entered undefended Avranches, finding both Sée bridges intact; Wikipedia gives the same date for VIII Corps.

current_activity: passing to Third Army and starting the Brittany operation
notes: Third Army became operational at noon on 1 August with VIII Corps assigned; CMH tables show 6th Armored and 83rd Divisions under VIII Corps / Third Army on 1 August.
Breakout-21 p410 describes the interior of the citadel after the surrender; Wikipedia dates the surrender to 17 August. Cézembre held out afterwards.

current_activity: opening the main attack on Brest with 29th, 8th and 2nd Divisions
notes: Breakout-30 p641: Middleton set the main attack for the afternoon of 25 August with 29th Division on the right, 8th in the center and 2nd on the left.

current_activity: passing from Third Army to Ninth Army control
notes: Event date: Breakout-30 p636 places the transfer on 10 September, five days after Ninth Army became operational at Rennes. Event definition: VIII Corps passes to Ninth Army operational control (preferred); the 5 September row (alternate) is the assignment-table date. Relationship: operational_control from 10 September. Location: the Brest sector; the corps headquarters is not located.

current_activity: receiving the capitulation of German forces in eastern Brest and Recouvrance
notes: Event date: Breakout-30 p650: both German capitulations at Brest occurred on 18 September (Recouvrance to the 29th Division, the east of the city to the 2nd Division); the garrison commanders were von der Mosel (29th Division sector) and Pietzonka (2nd Division sector). Event definition: surrender of the German forces holding Brest and Recouvrance. Ramcke, the fortress commander, had escaped to the Crozon peninsula and surrendered there on 19 September (see the alternate row), so the garrison did not surrender in a single act. Relationship: Ninth Army (VIII Corps passed to it on 10 September).

Event date: Wikipedia gives 19 September for the liberation of Brest. Event definition: 19 September is the day Ramcke surrendered on the Crozon peninsula, ending organised resistance in the Brest area (Breakout-30 p650); it is not a separate capture of the city, which capitulated on 18 September (preferred row). The point stays at Brest; Crozon is about 20 km to the south-west.

current_activity: corps headquarters and 2nd, 8th Divisions leaving Brest for Belgium and Luxembourg
notes: Breakout-30 p653: on 26 September VIII Corps headquarters and the 2nd and 8th Divisions began moving by rail and motor to Belgium and Luxembourg, still under Ninth Army; the 29th Division left for First Army on 24 September.
